item.title: Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100 Bitcoin price slipped near $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon, as Strategy (MSTR) and Coinbase (COIN) shares fell and traders waited on Nvidia’s first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. The bitcoin price had climbed back to about $65,000 before the U.S. open, after holding near that level on Monday. Selling picked up once stocks turned lower, and bitcoin price slipped to about $63,300 at its low. Strategy and Coinbase shares slide Strategy shares were recently down more than 5% to about $97, dropping below $100 and trading under the company’s STRC preferred stock, which was little changed near $99. It is the first time the common has traded below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is also down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close near $121. Strategy added 485 bitcoin last week, lifting its holdings to 850,849 BTC. The shares have kept falling with the bitcoin price. Coinbase was recently down about 3% to about $116. Robinhood (HOOD) and Circle (CRCL) dropped about 4% and 5%. Bitcoin miners were mostly lower. MARA Holdings (MARA), CleanSpark (CLSK) and IREN (IREN) each fell about 3% to 4%, and Cipher Mining (CIFR) was down about 2%. Hut 8 (HUT) was a modest exception, recently up about 1%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) were little changed, while Core Scientific (CORZ) and BitMine (BMNR) were also lower. Nvidia earnings weigh on stocks The broader market was also weaker late in the session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was recently down about 1.7%, after falling as much as about 1,000 points, or 2%, at its session low. The S&P 500 was down about 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite about 1%. Nvidia shares were recently down about 1.4%, after falling more than 3% earlier in the session. The chipmaker reports results after the bell, with analysts expecting revenue of about $109 billion. Interim CEO Colette Kress will lead her first earnings call in the role. Huang, in his first public statement since resigning last week, said he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided it was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America. Sources told CNBC on Monday that the board is not considering bringing him back. The bitcoin price bounced from its low as Nvidia shares pared some of their losses, and was recently near $64,000. What comes next for the bitcoin price New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that the AI investment boom could mean “we may need to raise rates more.” He played down a half-point hike in December. “I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action,” Williams said. Fed Governor Christopher Waller did not address the December decision in a payments speech Tuesday. Last week, he said a half-point hike should be considered if October’s core inflation ran at 0.3% or higher, and it did. Markets still point to a quarter-point increase at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting. item.title: Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale Situational Awareness, the artificial intelligence hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, cut its bitcoin miner holdings sharply in the third quarter, leaving about $80.8 million across three stocks and exiting three others, a Monday filing shows. The San Francisco firm still held 3,019,029 CleanSpark shares, worth $38.9 million at Sept. 30, 1,934,618 Bitdeer shares, worth $20.3 million, and 527,864 IREN shares, worth $21.6 million. Those are the only miner lines left, a sliver of the $1.83 billion in six miner stocks the fund listed at June 30. IREN Cut 94%, and three miners are gone The deepest cut was IREN. The fund held 9,474,099 IREN shares, worth $433.3 million, at midyear. The Sept. 30 stake is about 94% smaller by share count. CleanSpark was trimmed about 75%, from 12,276,139 shares worth $178.6 million. Bitdeer was reduced about 44%, from 3,439,450 shares worth $54.6 million. Bitdeer’s reported value fell further than its share count, to $20.3 million, as the stock also declined. Three names disappeared from the filing entirely. The fund had held 26,008,473 Core Scientific shares, worth $665.6 million, 17,100,000 Riot Platforms shares, worth $468.2 million, and 9,133,726 Hive Digital shares, worth $33.2 million, at June 30. None of those lines appear in the new report. The filing does not say whether those sales were part of a late-July portfolio sale, later trades, or both. An AI thesis that ran through Bitcoin miners Aschenbrenner published a long 2024 essay, “Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead,” arguing that artificial general intelligence was approaching faster than most investors appreciated, and that computing power and electricity would be the tight constraints. He founded the fund that September around that view, looking at technology and energy companies that AI would help or hurt. The miner stakes fit the same idea. A March profile described the fund as betting that electricity and computing capacity may be the most valuable assets in the AI build-out, pointing to miners that were turning high-density facilities and power contracts toward AI workloads. IREN has signed a multiyear cloud contract with Microsoft. CleanSpark has struck a $6.6 billion data-center lease. Listed miners have also been operating under tight economics this year, with bitcoin often trading below estimated production costs. A July sale to Citadel, then a much smaller filing The cuts landed after a brutal July. The fund sold the bulk of the fund’s public stock portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel late that month after heavy losses on AI-related holdings, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Those sources said the fund was forced to unwind most of its public book. item.title: Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives Coinbase launched an official plugin for ChatGPT on Tuesday that lets users connect a Coinbase account and trade bitcoin, other cryptocurrencies, stocks and derivatives without leaving the conversation, provided they approve every order. The company said the tool puts trading “in the same chat you use for everything else.” Users can connect an account, review a portfolio and place orders from ChatGPT on the web, on mobile or on desktop. Chief executive Brian Armstrong wrote that “starting today anyone with ChatGPT can connect their Coinbase account” and can “trade right inside your Coinbase account.” Coinbase posted a link to the official plugin in ChatGPT’s directory. Its developer documentation describes a short setup: sign in, review the access being requested and choose which portfolios the plugin can see. Interactive confirmation cards in the chat cover new orders, edits, cancellations and conversions between dollars and USDC. Read-only requests, such as checking a balance, do not use them. Bitcoin, Stocks and Dated Futures, With a Card on Every Trade The announcement did not single out bitcoin, but the plugin sits on the same rails as Coinbase for Agents, the company’s toolkit for connecting AI apps to a trading account. That documentation lists spot trading in more than 900 pairs, including bitcoin, along with eligible U.S. stocks and dated futures from Coinbase Financial Markets. The examples include a market buy of bitcoin and a dated bitcoin futures contract. Orders go through Advanced Trade, so those fees and eligibility rules apply. Fees vary by product, fee tier and whether an order adds or takes liquidity, and they are shown on the order preview. The official plugin is narrower than the full agent toolkit. A separate custom connection is required for the company’s Global Derivatives products and for x402 payments, which agents can use to buy market data. Coinbase already offers U.S. customers stock and ETF trading on its own platform, but the agent documentation says equity orders trade during regular market hours by default. The plugin should not be read as a new around-the-clock stock venue. What a user can buy still depends on the products already attached to that account. Official Access Is Limited to U.S. Coinbase Users Armstrong’s “anyone with ChatGPT” line is broader than the documentation. The official plugin is currently available to U.S. Coinbase users, and availability also depends on a user’s ChatGPT account and workspace. If the plugin does not appear, the company tells users to check their workspace’s plugin policy. In a disclaimer attached to Tuesday’s announcement, it said product availability, eligibility and Coinbase entities “vary by jurisdiction,” that trading can result in a total loss, and that “AI agents may fail.” The same post said users direct all AI activity and assume full responsibility. item.title: Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls Trezor said Monday that a data breach at Skladon, one of its shipping partners, exposed personal information tied to about 27,000 hardware-wallet orders, and that some customers have already reported scam calls. The company’s own systems were not compromised, and no wallet backups, PINs or passphrases were involved. Skladon notified Trezor on Nov. 15 of unauthorized access to systems that held customer shipping data. The breach itself took place on Nov. 7. Trezor believes the attacker exported records for orders placed between Aug. 9 and Nov. 7. An investigation is ongoing. Names, addresses and purchase details were leaked The exposed records included full names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses, order dates, and the products purchased and their prices. Trezor said neither it nor Skladon ever holds wallet backups, PINs or passphrases, so the breach does not, by itself, let an attacker move a buyer’s bitcoin. It does give a stranger a home address and proof that the person bought a device designed to store crypto. Anyone who received Trezor’s incident email and ordered in that window was affected. A small number of customers who ordered between Aug. 9 and 14 may also be included, but the company cannot email them because those details had already been anonymized under its 90-day retention policy. It is reaching those buyers through its blog and posted the same warning on X. Skladon does not ship to the United States, Trezor said, so U.S. customers were not affected by this incident. The company added that Skladon delivers to many countries, and that the leak is not limited to one region. Trezor warns of scam calls Trezor told customers to treat any unexpected call, text, email or letter about their order as suspicious, and to be alert to potential risks to their physical security. Scammers may quote real order details, including what was bought and what was paid, to make a message look genuine. Some customers have already reported scam calls. “Trezor will never cold-call you or ask for your wallet backup,” the company said . Customers should contact support only through the company’s website, never through a link, QR code or number in an unsolicited message, and should never enter a wallet backup anywhere except on their device. If a message contains a threat or makes someone feel unsafe, Trezor said to contact local police first. The third partner incident this year This is not the first time a Trezor contractor has lost customer data. In August, a breach at shipping provider ShipMonk exposed records from 13,689 customers, including 11,742 with full names, emails, phone numbers and shipping addresses. Trezor later said another approximately 67,000 U.S. customers who ordered between November 2019 and August 2021 were also affected, after ShipMonk failed to delete records it had assured the company were gone. item.title: Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion Wells Fargo more than doubled its holdings of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust in the third quarter to 49.6 million shares worth $2.35 billion at Sept. 30, though bitcoin’s slide since then has cut the stake’s value to about $1.82 billion. The bank disclosed the position in a Form 13F filed Monday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. It reported 49,577,094 IBIT shares across five of its units, up from 24,396,222 shares worth $812.2 million in its filing for June 30. That is an increase of about 103% in share count. The reported value rose about 189%, because IBIT climbed from $33.29 to $47.34 a share during the quarter. The fund closed at $36.79 on Monday. At that price, the same 49.6 million shares are worth roughly $1.82 billion, about $520 million less than the value in the filing. JUST IN: Wells Fargo disclosed 49.6 million shares of BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin ETF currently worth $1.82 billion, making them the largest institutional BTC ETF holder. That’s an ~200% increase from 24.4 million shares in Q2! pic.twitter.com/1GpMFeB8Ow — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 16, 2026 Mostly client accounts, not a house bet The filing does not break out how much of the position belongs to the bank and how much to its customers. But the largest single block, 32,483,714 shares worth about $1.54 billion, sits under Wells Fargo Clearing Services, the brokerage entity behind Wells Fargo Advisors. Wells Fargo Advisors Financial Network reported another 9.5 million shares, and Wells Fargo Bank reported 7.4 million. That points to a position built largely by wealth-management clients buying the ETF in brokerage and advisory accounts, rather than a directional trade by the bank itself. A 13F lists securities over which a firm has investment discretion, which at a big bank includes managed client money. Wells Fargo Securities, the investment-banking and trading arm, also reported IBIT options: calls on 717,200 shares and puts on 540,000 shares, valued at about $34.0 million and $25.6 million. Those figures reflect the value of the underlying shares, not the premiums paid, and they may hedge other positions. Both lines were smaller than at midyear, when the unit listed calls on 1.12 million shares and puts on 845,000. Wells Fargo also added to its other spot bitcoin funds. Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust rose to 3.09 million shares, worth $114.1 million, from 2.56 million. Bitwise’s bitcoin ETF rose to 1.6 million shares, worth $72.6 million, from 1.38 million. Strategy stake cut by a third The bank moved the other way on Strategy (MSTR). Wells Fargo’s long position in the bitcoin treasury company fell to 1,339,018 shares, worth $205.0 million at Sept. 30, from 1,994,253 shares at midyear, a drop of about 33%. item.title: Goldman Sachs More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Holdings to $1.28 Billion
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Goldman Sachs More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Holdings to $1.28 Billion Goldman Sachs more than doubled its spot bitcoin ETF holdings in the third quarter to about $1.28 billion, driven by a 52-fold jump in Fidelity’s fund, while cutting its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by more than half, a Monday filing shows. The bank reported the positions in a Form 13F covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. Its long holdings across five spot bitcoin funds were valued at $1.283 billion, up from about $580 million in its filing for June 30, an increase of roughly 121%. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust remained Goldman’s largest bitcoin fund holding, at 16,440,599 shares worth $778.3 million. The share count actually slipped about 5% from 17,232,201 at midyear. The value rose because IBIT climbed from $33.29 to $47.34 a share during the quarter, a gain of about 42%. The bigger change was in the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund. Goldman held 5,477,583 FBTC shares worth $397.9 million at Sept. 30, up from just 105,840 shares, worth $5.4 million, three months earlier. A new stake in Morgan Stanley’s bitcoin fund Goldman also reported 2,000,020 shares of the Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust, worth $47.9 million. The fund, ticker MSBT, launched in April as the first bitcoin product from a U.S. bank-affiliated asset manager, with a 0.14% sponsor fee. Goldman’s June filing did not list it. The trust reported 36.42 million shares outstanding and $873.4 million in net assets at Sept. 30, so Goldman held about 5.5% of the fund. The rest of the bitcoin fund book was smaller. Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust rose to 1,383,498 shares, worth $51.1 million, from 22,905. Goldman also listed 120,600 shares of the Grayscale Bitcoin Trust, worth $7.8 million, alongside puts on the same number of shares, which suggests that position is hedged. The bank’s options book in IBIT is large, too. It reported puts on 7,513,000 IBIT shares, valued at $355.7 million, and calls on 4,895,600 shares, valued at $231.8 million. Those figures reflect the value of the underlying shares, not premiums paid, so they do not measure money at risk. Goldman runs one of Wall Street’s biggest market-making and derivatives businesses, and its 13F does not say which positions are hedges for clients and which are its own views. Strategy shares cut, Strategy puts held The bank went the other way on Strategy. Goldman’s long position in the bitcoin treasury company fell to 2,760,766 shares, worth $422.6 million at Sept. 30, from 5,810,162 shares at midyear, a drop of about 52%. Its Strategy put options barely moved, covering 4,738,700 shares worth $725.4 million, compared with 4,735,800 in June. Calls rose to 707,200 shares from 575,900. Strategy closed at $103.03 on Monday, down from $153.09 at the end of September, as the company keeps buying bitcoin and buying back preferred stock. item.title: Bitcoin Policy Institute Renames to Finney Foundation for Open Technology
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Policy Institute Renames to Finney Foundation for Open Technology The Bitcoin Policy Institute announced Tuesday that it is now the Finney Foundation for Open Technology, a new parent organization whose brief spans open-source artificial intelligence, digital cash and encrypted messaging. The institute’s bitcoin work continues inside the foundation, and bitcoin remains a primary focus. The name honors Hal Finney (1956-2014), a cryptographer and software developer who helped build the email encryption program PGP, ran one of the first anonymous remailers and received the first bitcoin transaction from Satoshi Nakamoto in January 2009. In a November 1992 essay, Finney wrote that the computer “can be used as a tool to liberate and protect people, rather than to control them.” He was diagnosed with ALS the same year he received that first transaction and died in 2014. The Foundation’s case for open systems Washington is now writing the rules for artificial intelligence, the foundation said, and fear drives much of that debate. As the Bitcoin Policy Institute did for bitcoin, the Finney Foundation said it will argue that open systems outcompete closed ones, that individuals should control the tools they rely on, and that American strength comes from building in the open. “We set out to make Washington think about Bitcoin differently — to educate them on the importance of open monetary networks,” said David Zell, president of the Finney Foundation. “Our fellows now serve in congressional offices for both parties and in the executive branch. Our ideas have shaped discourse and policy. Our expansion will help us stay at the forefront of today’s most consequential policy debates, especially those around open source AI.” That argument was already on stage in September at Freedom Tech DC, the institute’s Washington summit, formerly the Bitcoin Policy Summit. The invite-only gathering put open-source and open-weight AI, data centers and energy infrastructure on the agenda alongside bitcoin and dollar-backed stablecoins. Block co-founder Jack Dorsey said there that “the next and probably largest element [of freedom technology] is open intelligence and making sure that it’s not locked up in the hands of any one government or any one company… that’s where we’re going to get the best outcomes.” A declaration and a new class of fellows Alongside the new name, the foundation published an Open Technology Declaration, titled “For Us, Not Over Us,” which argues for machines that serve people rather than rule over them. The text takes up Finney’s line about computers as tools of liberation and says the foundation will offer research, policy ideas and educational programs aimed at that goal. It asks who the new machines are for and who is in control of them, and it calls for people to build the tools they need without waiting for permission.
